content_voiceover: Within pediatric hemato-oncology itself, here's how question topics tend to distribute across diseases. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia is by far the most heavily tested single disease, with heavy emphasis on treatment, genetic and molecular analysis, and diagnosis, so this deserves the bulk of your preparation time. Acute myeloid leukemia comes next in frequency. Neuroblastoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, and Langerhans cell histiocytosis show up with questions clustered around treatment and diagnosis rather than deep molecular detail. Across all of these diseases, expect recurring questions on treatment-related complications and molecular risk stratification, since these cross-cutting themes get tested repeatedly regardless of which specific tumor is in the vignette.
keypoints: ALL is the single most tested disease: treatment, genetics, diagnosis
AML is the second most common topic
Neuroblastoma, HL, LCH: emphasis on diagnosis and treatment
Treatment complications and molecular risk are recurring cross-cutting themes
keypoint_voiceover: If you remember one thing from this slide, it's to prioritize ALL, followed by AML, then round out your prep with neuroblastoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, and LCH, while staying alert for treatment complication and molecular risk questions across all of them.
